title: Could a Neuroscientist Understand a Microprocessor?
description: Research article (PLOS Computational Biology 13(1): e1005268, published January 12, 2017) that treats a simulated classic microprocessor, a system that is complex and fully understood at every level, as a model organism and applies popular neuroscience analyses to it: connectomics, lesioning single transistors, tuning curves, pairwise and global correlations, local field potentials, Granger causality and dimensionality reduction. It asks whether these analyses recover how the processor works and discusses what understanding a system should mean.
